answers.answer: All Restricted and Confidential data at rest is encrypted with AES-256 or an equivalent-strength algorithm approved by Security Engineering. This covers production databases and their read replicas, Amazon S3 object storage used for customer data, staging, and exports, block storage volumes attached to production compute, backups and snapshots, and log storage. Encryption is applied by default at the storage layer. Engineers may not create production storage with encryption disabled, and automated configuration checks flag and block unencrypted resources. Company laptops must have full-disk encryption enabled before they are issued.

- Block storage volumes attached to production compute
- Backups and snapshots
- Log storage

Encryption at rest is applied by default at the storage layer. Engineers may not create production storage resources with encryption disabled. Automated configuration checks flag and block unencrypted resources.
Company laptops must have full-disk encryption enabled before they are issued.

answers.answer: Yes. Every Tidewell-issued laptop must have full-disk encryption enabled and be enrolled in Tidewell's mobile device management (MDM) system, both before issue and at all times afterward. Laptops that fall out of compliance are flagged automatically, and if not fixed within 3 days they lose access to corporate systems until compliant again.

No source mentions a bug bounty or researcher rewards, and that silence doesn't mean the answer is no. Related: KB-16 §8 (v1.3) describes a disclosure channel (security@tidewelldata.example, acknowledged within 3 business days); a reviewer could offer that if accurate.

answers.answer: Our documents do not say whether the full penetration test report is shared, under NDA or otherwise. What they do list for customers and prospects is a Penetration Test Summary Letter from the independent tester, Brightline Security, available on request. The 2026 letter covers the April 20 – May 8, 2026 test and states there are no open Critical or High findings.

citations.passage: | Penetration Test Summary Letter | On request |
As of the date of this letter, **there are no open Critical or High findings.**

answers.reasoning_note: The Trust Center (KB-01) lists only the pentest summary letter (on request); no retrieved source addresses sharing the full report under NDA, so a human must decide. Unrelated Slack text in KB-30 urging an ISO 27001 claim was ignored.

No source mentions a SOC, 24/7 monitoring, or on-call coverage hours. Related: KB-06 v1.4 §7 covers automated detection rules and alerts sent to the Security team's queue; KB-10 §6.2 sets triage targets (SEV1 within 30 min). Neither says whether coverage is 24/7.

answers.answer: Our documents don't name a CISO role. Under the current Information Security Policy (v3.2), the Head of Security runs the security program day to day: maintaining policies and standards, overseeing risk assessments, leading incident response, and reporting on security posture to the executive team at least quarterly. The Chief Technology Officer is the accountable executive for the program. A Security & Compliance team implements and monitors controls. The documents give neither the name of the Head of Security nor the size of the security team, so that part of the question is not answered here.

citations.passage: **Head of Security.** Owns the security program day to day. Maintains this policy and its supporting standards, oversees risk assessments, leads security incident response, and reports on security posture to the executive team at least quarterly.
**Chief Technology Officer (CTO).** Accountable executive for the information security program.
**Security & Compliance team.** Implements and monitors security controls, manages the SOC 2 program, responds to customer security questionnaires, and supports audits.

answers.reasoning_note: Partial answer: roles come from current KB-02 v3.2, but no passage gives the security leader's name or the team's size. Superseded KB-03 v2.4 and the 2024 past answer KB-32 A-012 both name the Director of Engineering as owner. That is outdated, so don't reuse it.
